docs.title: Skylords Reborn Blender Artist Guides
docs.text:
Create and export models with SR-ImpEx. These guides describe the upcoming V4 development build. V4 is not released yet; the current public release may look different or lack some of the features shown here.

Start here: Object Guide — create or edit static and animated props from an existing DRS, a new model or a foreign model.

  • Default Material Guide
  • Unit Guide
  • Building Guide
  • Modules, Debris & Resources
  • Shading Recipes
  • Locator Guide
  • Animation Set Guide
  • Effect Set Guide

docs.title: Advanced Tutorials
docs.text:
• Animation: cast/recovery, multiple hits and channelled phases.
  • Effects: timed layers, attached fire, fades and previews.
  • IK: engine limits and baking Blender IK onto an export rig.

Select a screenshot to open it at full size.

docs.title: Animation Set Guide
docs.text:
Assign your model's Actions to the animations used by the game. Finish your mesh, materials and rig first. For animated props, see the Object Guide.

For worked casts, multiple hit moments and channelled abilities, use the Advanced Animation Tutorial.

docs.title: 1. Assign animations
docs.text:
1. Select your model and open DRS Editor → Animation Set Editor.
  2. For a new model, click Init or Initialize Animation Set and choose its type.
  3. Select an entry and assign its Animation (SKA).
  4. Check it with Play.
  5. Click Save. Save the .blend separately.

Switching between models keeps each model's pending animation edits and selected entry for this Blender session. Click Save on each edited model before exporting or saving your .blend. Reset reloads that model's saved settings; opening a .blend starts from saved settings too.

In a narrow sidebar, click the current animation name beside the search icon and type to choose another mapping. + opens Add Ability; − removes the selected mapping. Widen the sidebar for the full mapping list.

Model type Starting entries Static Object None Animated Object Idle Unit Idle, Walk, Run, Spawn, Die Building Idle when there is an armature

Use Add Ability for animations already used by the unit's game setup. This assigns animations; it does not create a new gameplay ability.

For a new ability:

  1. Click + → Ability (Cast / Resolve) for a cast and recovery, or Ability (Start / Loop / End) for a sustained action.
  2. Select the new Ability entry and give it a name, such as Summon.
  3. Assign its Actions and set the phase boundaries. Press Play to check them.
  4. Note the Game animation tag shown in the entry. The game ability must use this tag and the matching Cast/Resolve or Start/Loop/End gameplay jobs.
  5. Click Save. Add another entry for another ability, then save your .blend.

The editor chooses an available existing animation slot. The DRS export does not change the game's ability definition or create an ability. The game stores IDs rather than the custom name, so reimporting a DRS does not restore the name. If no compatible slot is available, the option is disabled. Test the ability with its game setup before use.

Choosing a basic animation

The picker offers Idle, Walk, Run, Spawn, Death, Attack, directional Hit, Knockdown / Get Up and Cheer / Emote, plus Cast and the two ability layouts. Existing model type restrictions still apply.

Transitions between animations

The game normally blends from one animation into the next using its own crossfade settings. On the ordinary Cast / Resolve path, a custom ability uses the general Cast and Resolve transition rules even when its animation slot has a specific game name. You do not need to add a crossfade animation.

The game's ability must still use the displayed tag and compatible jobs. Different mappings can use different playback types, so check the ability and its transitions in the Map Editor or game. Blender's Play controls do not reproduce the full game transition system.

Existing game-specific mappings are available in Debug View. Use those when matching a unit's existing game setup. Blender playback does not simulate the game ability; test the exported animation with its matching game setup.

An imported entry shown as Animation … (unidentified) is kept on export. Keep it unless you know it is not needed by the model's game setup.

For TombOfDeath, the Start, Loop and End slots are available, but automatic gameplay timing is not verified. Check the timings with the game's setup.

Choose the Mode used by the unit's game setup. Base, Mode 1 and Mode 2 are separate animation banks. Mode 1 and Mode 2 do not mean entering and leaving a mode.

Keep a working Base Idle for units. Several missing animations fall back to it. Loading the model does not prove every action can play safely.

For alternative animations, assign each variant an Action and weights such as 80 / 20, totaling 100%. These are percentage chances. Use Normalize to 100% when shown to calculate them while keeping the proportions. Check every variant. Unassigned variants are not exported.

docs.title: 2. Check the clip
docs.text:
Open Clip Settings → Edit Settings to change FPS, looping and interpolation. For a keyed Action, edit its keys to change the length, then confirm with OK. The range is calculated from those keys; imported end padding is kept. Without keys, the stored range is editable. Settings belong to the Action and are shared by entries using it.

Changing FPS changes duration without moving keys. It does not change Blender's rendering performance. Play sets the scene's clip range and frame rate.

Keep Allows IK enabled when the game should use procedural IK during this clip. Use Force No Blend only when normal pose blending is unwanted.

docs.title: 3. Set the release moment
docs.text:
For one Action containing both preparation and recovery:

  1. Add the matching cast entry and choose One Clip.
  2. Assign one Action containing the whole motion.
  3. Set Cast→Resolve to the release moment.
  4. Check Play Cast and Play Resolve, then Save.

Cast is preparation before releasing the spell or shot. Resolve is the recovery afterward: draw the bow, release the arrow, then lower the bow.

For a 1.2-second Action releasing at 0.3 seconds, use 0.25. Cast lasts 0.3 seconds; recovery lasts 0.9 seconds. You do not need two SKA files.

Spawn and Idle do not need an artificial Cast/Resolve pair. Keep the entries used by the existing gameplay ability.

A Spawn Action can contain several visual stages, such as appearing, rising and landing. Keep them in one clip. Adding Spawn variants creates alternatives, not a sequence of stages.

For a channelled ability, Start / Loop / End let the middle section repeat until gameplay ends the ability. Use the phases required by that ability; splitting an Action alone does not add gameplay phases.

docs.title: Separate clips
docs.text:
Choose Separate Clips to assign a different Action to each phase. Assign Cast and Resolve, check each with Play, then Save. Each phase uses its whole clip; change Range Start / End only to trim it. For independent clips, trimming the Actions themselves is safest: disjoint ranges can change the engine's phase timing order.

For example, a 0.4-second Cast and 0.8-second Resolve release at 0.4 seconds and finish at 1.2 seconds. Timing is calculated automatically. Start / Loop / End sets offer the same clip choice. Keep corresponding variant counts and weights aligned; editing a phase's variant weight updates the matching phases.

Switching clip layout resets phase ranges. Imported separate clips stay separate. For Ground & Air casts, keep their release and total durations matching.

docs.title: 4. Place a spawn or attack marker
docs.text:
1. Select the variant and click Edit Markers.
  2. Choose a marker and set Time: 0.5 means halfway through the whole Action.
  3. Use + / − to add or remove markers. Confirm with OK.
  4. Click Display Marker to inspect the selected marker's pose.
  5. Move or rotate the helper in Object Mode, then click Save Placement.
  6. Click Save for the animation set.

Direction can affect gameplay. A melee marker can steer pushback as well as visual hit reactions. Keep imported directions unless you want to change the attack's response.

For ordinary attacker-to-target pushback, set Direction to 0, 0, 0. The helper becomes a sphere because it has no direction. New markers use this neutral setting.

Moving the helper edits its stored Position. The verified timing-generation path does not use that position as the impact location. Use a locator for a projectile or attached effect: see the Locator Guide.

All markers are editable. For an attack with several hit moments, add one marker per moment. Their gameplay timings are generated when saving. The unit's gameplay ability must also support those events; extra markers alone do not create new attacks or effects. Removing all markers leaves an empty list.

Timing readout

Cast (ms) is the event offset. Duration (ms) includes the whole animation. For 300 / 1200 ms, recovery is 900 ms.

Markers and EffectSet events are separate. To align them, use the same Action and time fraction. A marker does not create an effect by itself.

New or edited markers generate gameplay timings from the marker time and clip duration when you save. Unchanged imported timings are preserved. After changing only a clip's length or FPS, check the timing readout: an existing marker's timing may not be rebuilt automatically. If necessary, edit the marker and save the animation set again. Custom timing overrides remain fixed until you change or disable them.

SKA text events such as <blink> are a separate feature under the selected animation's Advanced SKA Data. They are not these gameplay markers or Effect Set events. Their use in Skylords still needs practical testing.

Advanced: custom gameplay timing

Click Edit Markers (or Edit Events where shown) and enable Custom Gameplay Timings to add, remove or edit timing records directly. Event (ms) is the trigger moment; Total (ms) includes recovery. Keep the event within that total.

These overrides stay fixed when clip lengths change. Disable the option to return to timings generated from markers or phases. Verify custom timing in the Map Editor with the matching gameplay ability.

docs.title: 5. Adjust motion settings when needed
docs.text:
Keep imported settings unless you intend to change the model's response in-game. In a narrow sidebar, open Motion Settings to edit these controls.

Setting Use Walk / Run Reference Speed Match the speed each movement clip was authored for; this does not set gameplay speed. Partial Mode Change Keep the established setting for units with mode transitions. Align to Terrain Let a ground unit tilt with the terrain. Flight → Hovering Ground Unit Configure hovering motion and its matching pushback response; this does not grant flight. Turn Banking / Movement Pitch / Hit Displacement Adjust a flying or hovering unit's visual motion response.

You do not need to enter Timing Attribute IDs. Changing Hovering Ground Unit also updates its matching runtime attribute. Other imported attributes are retained.

docs.title: 6. Edit IK limits when needed
docs.text:
Open IK Limits and select a bone on the deform armature in Pose Mode.

  1. Click Add IK Limits, or Edit Angle Limits for an imported entry.
  2. Choose Look At, Curve Walking, or both for the intended engine IK use.
  3. Keep imported axes, Inverted and Chain Order settings unless you are deliberately rebuilding the IK chain.
  4. Edit the enabled X/Y/Z angle limits. Open Advanced IK Settings for chain order, inversion and damping.
  5. Export the model. Bone IK settings are read directly during export.

Remove IK Limits removes that bone's exported IK entry.

The game supplies procedural targets and movement state. Regular Blender playback does not reproduce the complete engine IK controller. The generated limit constraint is muted so it does not constrain every keyframed pose. For motion that must play exactly in Blender and the SKA, bake it onto deform bones. The Advanced IK Tutorial covers both workflows.

docs.title: 7. Export and check
docs.text:
1. Click Save in the Animation Set Editor and save the .blend.
  2. Bake control-rig or constraint-driven motion onto the deform rig when needed.
  3. Export the DRS and its intended SKA Actions together.
  4. Check Idle, movement, release timing and pushback in the Map Editor.
Imported root alignment and metadata

Keep the imported rig's rest pose and root alignment. The plugin preserves its additional root transform, called SuperParent. Do not add an extra bone with that name. After changing the rest pose, export matching DRS and animation files together.

You do not need to create metadata hashes or UUIDs. Keep imported metadata; the exporter supplies the structure for new models.

For sound and visual effects, continue with the Effect Set Guide.

docs.title: Effect Set Guide
docs.text:
Add existing sounds and visual effects to a model's animations. Create or edit the effects themselves in the external Effect Editor.

For timed sound/FX layers, fading attached effects and controller previews, follow the Advanced Effects Tutorial.

For continuous fire or smoke, use a persistent locator. For building destruction, use Damage Preview.

docs.title: 1. Set the library folder
docs.text:
Open Edit → Preferences → Add-ons → SR ImpEx.

  • Set Skylords Reborn Folder to your game installation, containing base/pak.
  • Leave Effects Folder empty for installed game assets. Set it to a loose asset folder when testing your own effects.

The paths are saved automatically. The first search builds an index; later searches reuse it. Use Refresh Effect Library if an asset is missing after you add or replace files.

Switching models keeps pending event edits and the selected event/resource for this Blender session. Click Save for each edited model before exporting or saving the .blend. Reset reloads that model's saved EffectSet.

docs.title: 2. Add an event
docs.text:
1. Select your model and open DRS Editor → Effect Set Editor.
  2. Add an entry and choose its Action.
  3. Under Events, click + and choose its Type from the table below.
  4. Set Time: 0 is the clip's start, 0.5 its middle and 1 its end.
  5. Under Resources, choose a resource alternative and open Effect Selector.
  6. Search for a resource, select it and click Use Resource.
  7. Use one variant at Chance 100% while testing.
  8. Click Save, then save your .blend.

A new animation entry uses the Action currently assigned to the model's armature. Use the clock button beside Time to copy the playhead's position within that Action. Play the same Action on the model first.

Type Use it to Sound Play a sound. World FX Spawn an effect at the model's position, with an offset. Linked FX Play an effect using its own source/target attachment setup. Fade Out Persistent FX Fade out an existing locator effect with that resource name. Fade In Persistent FX Fade that persistent effect back in.

For fades, set Fade Duration (s). These events affect an existing effect; they do not spawn a new one. For other FX events, Offset adjusts placement. Use a locator when an effect needs a particular bone attachment.

docs.title: 3. Choose a resource
docs.text:
In Effect Selector, search at the top or choose a category on the left. Use All Resources if you cannot find a name. Sound events show audio resources.

Preview auditions the selected resource. Use Resource assigns it to the editable filename field; Cancel keeps the previous resource. Save the EffectSet or apply the locator changes afterward.

docs.title: 4. Play and adjust
docs.text:
1. In Object Mode, click Update Preview.
  2. Press Space to play the normal timeline.
  3. Adjust timing, resource, volume, pitch or offset. Live Update applies changes after a short pause in editing.
  4. Click Save when you are happy with the result.

Use Effects to switch the whole model's FX preview on or off. Off also mutes its sounds; the model animation continues. Use Sound to mute just the preview audio. These switches also apply to locator FX, take effect immediately and do not change exports. Switching on reuses the cached preview at the current frame.

Selected Variant auditions the highlighted resource; Engine Chances uses the saved chances. × beside Update Preview removes the generated preview instead of hiding it. Rebuild after reopening a .blend.

An imported effect has no loaded Action

Some models retain effect entries for clips that their Animation Set does not use. The list still shows the stored filename; the events are preserved. For example, Vulcan retains run_flamethrower1 and spawn_shadowflame_demon1. To inspect extra clips, import the DRS with Other Clips in Folder enabled. You do not need to assign a different animation just to remove the notice.

For an event that must line up with an attack, use the same Action and time fraction as its animation marker. A marker does not create an effect by itself.

docs.title: Variants and chances
docs.text:
Variants are alternatives. Use 80 / 20 for two choices, or 40 / 30 / 30 for three. These total 100%, so one resource is always chosen.

4 / 3 / 3 leaves 90% silence or no effect. Click Normalize to 100% to keep those proportions but play a resource every time. Avoid totals above 100%.

To play two resources together, add two events at the same Time, each with its own resource variant.

docs.title: 5. Export and test
docs.text:
1. Save EffectSet and AnimationSet changes, then save your .blend.
  2. Export with Include Animation Files to include referenced animation clips.
  3. Install custom effects, textures and sounds separately alongside their dependencies.
  4. Reimport a copy of the model, then test the result in the Map Editor.
Advanced: sound controls

Volume adjusts the cue. Pitch Min / Max vary its playback rate: 0 is unchanged, 0.1 is 10% faster, and -0.1 is 10% slower. Duration changes too.

Fields marked Export Only are saved for the game. Spatial falloff needs positional audio; interruptible cues need gameplay interruptions. Check those behaviours in the Map Editor or game. Open Game Playback to edit falloff and interruption settings. The preserved Condition is only shown in Debug View.

To create overlapping sound layers, use separate events. Variants choose alternatives; they do not mix several sounds together.

Advanced: preview limits

Blender previews particles, effect meshes, lights, trails, decals, effect animation controllers and cached debris. Some appearances and gameplay responses still differ from the game.

Feature How to check it Refraction meshes Update Preview, add a render setup with Add Render, then press F12. The viewport uses simpler shading. Check overlapping haze in the Map Editor. Glow Added automatically for supported effects. Compare its final brightness in the Map Editor. Billboard masks Loaded automatically with the effect. Their alpha controls visibility; the mask stays in place while the color texture animates. Terrain contacts Add a terrain mesh outside the model's export collection, then rebuild the preview. Without one, the preview uses flat ground. Debris and particle motion Rebuild after changing the model animation or environment. Playback reuses cached motion. Dense effects Preview counts and sampling can be reduced. Read Effect Preview Report for this resource. Heat haze, scene fog, water waves and advanced links Parts remain incomplete. Use the Map Editor for the final check. Camera shake Reported without moving your camera.

Read the model's Effect Preview Report in Blender's Text Editor for missing dependencies and unsupported components. Do not edit generated preview objects; edit the reference or the original effect and rebuild.

Troubleshooting Problem Check No previewable resources Check the selected Action, resource paths and Audio toggle. A clip without events, or a chance of silence, can be valid. Resource not found Check folders, filename and dependencies. Some sounds use an XML sound set or an SNR/SNS pair. Ambiguous resource name Use a unique resource name or remove duplicate test assets from your library. Effect appears at the wrong pose Time is a fraction of the whole clip, not seconds or a frame number. One animation variant has no effect Add an entry for each SKA clip that needs it. Fade has no effect Check that a persistent locator uses the matching resource name. Effects lag behind your edits Wait for a rebuild to finish. Large effects take longer. Updates wait until rendering ends. An effect needs its own animated rig Keep its referenced DRS and SKA in the library. Update Preview loads the supported controller automatically.

Continue with the Animation Set Guide for action mappings, or the Locator Guide for attachment points.

docs.title: Locator Editor
docs.text:
Locators are attachment points for effects, projectiles, health bars and model parts.

Use a locator for where an effect or projectile is attached. Use an animation marker for when a supported gameplay event occurs; adding a locator alone does not create that event. See the Animation Set Guide.

docs.title: Edit a locator
docs.text:
1. Select your model and open DRS Editor → Locator Editor.
  2. Select a locator in the list, or click + beside the list and choose its type.
  3. Choose Attach to. For a resource locator, select its Effect or Resource.
  4. Click Apply Changes.
  5. Move or rotate the marker in the viewport, then click Save Placement.
  6. Save your .blend and export the model.

The list stays short; scroll to see more entries. − beside the list removes the selected locator record and its marker. Only relevant fields appear below the list. Hover over Attach to for a description of each choice.

Changing an attachment starts the locator at its new attachment's origin. Changing only its type or filename keeps its placement. Apply pending detail edits before saving placement.

docs.title: Choose an attachment
docs.text:
Choice What it means Model Moves with the model, without following a particular bone. Skeleton Gives the effect access to the model's skeleton, so the effect can use its own bone links. Bone Follows the bone you choose.

For imported models, keep the original attachment unless you intend to change it. Skeleton does not mean the first or root bone. Firedancer uses it for one persistent effect whose internal emitters attach to her head and hands.

Imported attachments

Older lists use the same editor. Export selects the record layout needed for your changes. The former numeric options -1 and -2 are now Model and Skeleton; keep the imported choice unless changing the attachment.

docs.title: Choose and preview an effect
docs.text:
1. Configure Skylords Reborn Folder in the add-on preferences. See the Effects Guide.
  2. Select a Persistent Figure FX or Persistent Building FX locator.
  3. Click the search icon beside Effect to open Effect Selector. Search by name or choose a category.
  4. Preview auditions the resource. Use Resource updates the draft filename; Cancel keeps the previous one.
  5. Click Apply Changes, then Update Preview. Press Space to play the timeline.

Effects switches this model's cached FX preview on or off, including its sound. The model animation continues. Sound mutes only the preview audio. Both switches also control the same model's Effect Set previews and do not change exports. Live Update refreshes resource edits after you pause editing. × beside Update Preview removes the generated preview. State-triggered effects require the corresponding game state; they are not automatically played as persistent effects.

Firedancer's Idle fire comes from her persistent locator, not an Idle EffectSet entry. It can play without an animation event.

Categories are filename hints. The source effect files remain external assets; assigning a reference does not copy them into the DRS. Create or edit effects in the external Effect Editor.

docs.title: Placement and export
docs.text:
• Use +, rather than duplicating marker objects. Duplicated markers can share the same internal identity.
  • Use Save Placement after moving or rotating markers. Export uses saved locator data, not unsaved viewport movement.
  • Deleting a marker alone does not remove its saved locator. Use − beside the list.
  • Module references can show imported model parts. Changing a filename does not automatically rebuild construction geometry.
  • Preserve imported unknown types. IDs 14 and 15 are not offered for new locators.
  • Test attachments through representative animations and in the Map Editor after export.

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
Problem Check No locator list Select a mesh or collection belonging to the intended model. A bone attachment cannot be selected Import the model's skeleton first. A marker moves to the origin Changing attachment resets placement. Position it afterward and Save Placement. A locator returns after deleting its marker Remove the record with − beside the list. Export uses an old position Save Placement before exporting. The effect is missing Check the library path and resource filename, then Update Preview. Game-state FX may require their activation state.

See the Effects Guide for animation-triggered effects and sounds, and the Unit Guide for the full workflow.

docs.title: Shading Recipes
docs.text:
For ordinary solid surfaces, start with the Default Material Guide. These recipes cover cutouts, smooth transparency, flowing surfaces and reflections.

Select a mesh and open DRS Editor → Material Editor. Use Artist View. Keep an imported model's material type unless you intend to change its appearance.

docs.title: Cut-out leaves, fences and fabric
docs.text:
1. Use Default and assign the ColorMap.
  2. Put the cutout mask in ColorMap alpha: white is visible; black is a hole.
  3. Enable Material Flags → EnableAlphaTest.
  4. Inspect the edges, export a copy and check it in the Map Editor.

Alpha Test makes a visible-or-invisible cutout. Use the next recipe for a soft fade. Default's ParamMap alpha controls emissivity, so do not put the cutout mask there.

docs.title: A simple surface with smooth transparency
docs.text:
1. Choose SimpleTextured.
  2. Assign its Texture with an opacity gradient in the image alpha channel.
  3. Start with white Color, material Alpha 1 and UseVertexColor off.
  4. Use white alpha for visible areas, black for invisible areas and gray for partial opacity.
  5. Lower material Alpha to fade the whole surface further.

Keep alpha when saving the texture. If overlapping surfaces look wrong, try DisableDepthWrite while keeping depth testing enabled, then test in the Map Editor.

Switching to SimpleTextured changes the material's features. It does not keep Default's normal/PAR lighting or FluidMap flow. For a flowing waterfall, use the recipe below first.

docs.title: Lava and other flowing surfaces
docs.text:
1. Keep Default and assign its FluidMap.
  2. Assign the ParamMap; use its blue channel to mask where flow appears.
  3. Open Flow — Speed and Direction and enable Custom Flow Settings.
  4. Set Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed. Use matching values for steady movement.
  5. Adjust Pattern Scale, then press Space to play.

The body can stay still. Flow uses the timeline and continues across clip loops. Pause to hold it; scrub while paused to inspect a particular time.

Leaving Custom Flow Settings off uses the default movement. It does not disable flow.

Flow while rendering

Render frames use timeline time. The same frame gives the same flow pattern. A continuously playing viewport can look different after several animation loops.

docs.title: Reflections
docs.text:
1. Enable UseEnvironmentMap.
  2. Assign an EnvironmentMap, or choose Use Bundled Environment when shown.
  3. Use Render Setup → Add Render and inspect the whole model in Rendered shading.

The game's lighting and environment can differ. Check the final reflection in the intended map.

docs.title: Refraction and a soft-edged waterfall
docs.text:
For a waterfall that already flows, keep its Default material and FluidMap.

  1. Assign RefractionParamMap.
  2. Start with white RefractionColor and RefractionScale 0.
  3. Use neutral RG and black B in the refraction map for the first test.
  4. Increase its alpha near the soft edge to add the background there.
  5. Reduce the water contribution in that same area. Fade the ParamMap blue flow mask and check that the ColorMap and glow do not leave a solid edge.
  6. Disable Alpha Test for this soft-edge test.
  7. Check the edge before adding subtle distortion with RefractionScale.

Refraction-map alpha adds background; it does not automatically hide the water. Keep the rest of the material dark enough at the faded edge. Test the finished waterfall in the Map Editor.

Advanced: refraction texture channels

For this Default refraction setup, RG controls the background distortion, B contributes blur/mip bias, and alpha contributes filtered background.

The Blender camera preview reproduces part of this. The B-channel blur, overlapping layers and viewport appearance still differ from the game. For effects containing refraction meshes, Update Preview → Add Render → F12 gives the more complete supported preview. See the Effect Set Guide.

docs.title: Vertex-painted color
docs.text:
For a Textured or SimpleTextured material, use Create SR Vertex Colors. Paint the resulting SR Color0 attribute and keep the material's vertex-color flag enabled. Check the exported result in the Map Editor before relying on it for a new material setup.

Other material types and preview limits

The selector includes specialized effect, terrain and render-pass materials. Do not switch an ordinary model to one of these just to enable a single feature. Keep an imported material's type and edit its named slots.

Material family Current Blender workflow Default Use the Default Material Guide for its maps, flow, wind and supported surface parameters. Textured / SimpleTextured Edit their Texture, Color and supported flags. The Default PAR channel recipe does not apply. DiffuseSpecular variants Use their DiffuseMap and SpecularMap. The preview covers basic color/specular inputs, with approximate lighting. Lava / Effect Keep the source setup. Some base inputs are previewed; specialized procedural layers and shader behaviour are not fully reproduced. Billboard / ParticleSystem / StatefulParticles / Trail For particle motion and effect-controlled animation, use the FX preview. A material on a static mesh does not create an emitter. Decal, cliff, terrain, sky and UI families Basic routed textures may be visible; the game's projection, layering and scene passes are not recreated as a complete shader. Remaining specialized handlers Preserve the imported setup. A readable/exportable parameter is not proof of a matching visual preview.

Billboard: its Texture alpha controls transparency. Enable UseAlphaMask to multiply it by MaskTexture alpha. Mask colors do not tint the result. On a mesh, these textures use its UVs; the FX preview supplies the effect's camera-facing quad and separate mask coordinates.

Default distortion: assign a DistortionParamMap with gradients in its alpha channel. DistortionMeshScale moves the separate distortion surface along its normals. Blender approximates the distortion with refraction.

MonoColor uses Alpha for opacity. In VolumetricFog, the red channel of DensityMap varies the density. DensityMapInfluence controls how much of that pattern is visible.

Export only settings are saved and have no live preview. Default DepthWriteThreshold is in Debug View and affects depth writes during an engine fade. Engine effect unverified means the flag is registered and its visual effect in the engine has yet to be established.

Complete recipes and visual comparisons for every specialized material are still outstanding. The supported basic preview is useful for editing; it is not a replacement for the final engine check.

docs.title: Before sharing
docs.text:
1. Save painted images and your .blend.
  2. Export to a separate folder and review the log.
  3. Reimport the exported model and inspect its maps and transparency.
  4. Check the moving surface, reflections and edges in the Map Editor.
When the Blender preview differs Appearance Next check A slider has no effect Its value may come from a texture. Edit that map instead. A map does nothing Check the selected material type, slot checkbox and feature flag. Flow is static Press Space; check FluidMap and the blue flow mask. Soft transparency has hard edges Disable Alpha Test and use a material setup supporting smooth transparency. Refraction differs Compare a camera render and the Map Editor; blur and layered distortion are incomplete in Blender. Reflections or glow look different Compare the intended game lighting and environment.

docs.title: Advanced Animation Tutorial
docs.text:
Build a cast, a multi-hit attack or a channelled animation with the Animation Set Editor. Start with a model and working Actions on its deform armature. For the initial setup, use the Animation Set Guide.

In a narrow sidebar, click the selected mapping's name to search the current mode's animations. Ground/Air casts and phase groups remain grouped; select their phase buttons to edit Cast, Resolve, Start, Loop or End.

docs.title: One Action for a cast and its recovery
docs.text:
Example: a two-second Action raises a staff, releases a spell after half a second, then lowers the staff.

  1. Add the Cast ability used by the unit's game setup.
  2. Select its Cast entry and choose One Clip.
  3. Assign the complete Action.
  4. Set Cast→Resolve to 0.25: the release is one quarter through the Action.
  5. Check Play Cast, then Play Resolve.
  6. Click Save.

The release occurs at 0.5 seconds; the recovery lasts 1.5 seconds. The editor calculates both phase ranges and gameplay timings. You do not need to enter milliseconds or duplicate the Action.

For Ground & Air versions of the same ability, keep the release and total duration matching. Assign the corresponding motions to both entries.

The game needs the matching ability

Adding a Cast entry supplies animation data. It does not create a spell, projectile, damage event or new gameplay job.

docs.title: Separate Cast and Resolve Actions
docs.text:
Use this when preparation and recovery already exist as different Actions.

  1. Select the Cast entry and choose Separate Clips.
  2. Click Cast and assign the preparation Action.
  3. Click Resolve and assign the recovery Action.
  4. Keep Range Start / End at 0 / 1 to use each complete Action.
  5. Play each phase, then Save.

A 0.5-second Cast followed by a 1.5-second Resolve has the same release and total duration as the One Clip example. The chosen layout changes how you author the motion, not the ability's gameplay requirements.

Trim the Actions themselves when possible. Switching clip layout resets the phase ranges. Imported separate clips remain separate until you change them.

docs.title: An attack with two hit moments
docs.text:
Example: one Action swings twice, with hits at 30% and 70% of the clip.

  1. Select the matching Attack entry and its Action variant.
  2. Open Edit Markers.
  3. Add two markers and set Time to 0.3 and 0.7.
  4. Keep Direction at 0, 0, 0 for ordinary attacker-to-target pushback.
  5. Confirm with OK, then Save.

The timings are generated from the markers and clip duration. The gameplay ability must support both hits. Extra markers alone do not add damage.

After changing only clip length or FPS, check the timing readout. Unchanged imported timings may be preserved instead of recalculated; edit the marker and save again if an update is needed.

For a deliberate directional hit, use Display Marker, rotate its arrow and click Save Placement. Keep an imported direction unless you intend to change the hit response. Marker Position is stored, but it is not a projectile spawn locator. Use the Locator Editor for that.

Add matching sounds and visuals separately in the Effect Set Editor, using the same Action and Time. Follow the Advanced Effects Tutorial.

docs.title: Start / Loop / End for a channelled ability
docs.text:
Use this only for an ability whose game setup already supports these phases.

Phase Author this motion Start Enter the channelled pose. Loop Repeat the sustained motion with a clean seam. End Leave the pose and recover.

Choose One Clip and set the phase boundaries, or choose Separate Clips and assign an Action to each phase. Check the phase playback buttons and save. For separate clips, set the middle Action's Loop setting in Clip Settings.

A Spawn Action with several visual stages can stay in one clip. Adding three Spawn variants creates three alternatives, not a three-part sequence.

docs.title: Alternative motions and mode banks
docs.text:
• Add Action variants for different ways to perform the same animation. Their Weight values are percentage chances, such as 80 / 20; keep the assigned variants at 100% total. Use Normalize to 100% to keep their proportions and calculate those percentages automatically.
  • Matching Cast/Resolve or Start/Loop/End variants are kept together. Changing one phase's weight updates the corresponding phases.
  • Base, Mode 1 and Mode 2 are separate animation banks. Use the bank selected by the unit's game setup; they do not mean Start / Loop / End.
  • Keep a working Base Idle for units, including units with extra modes.

A total below 100% can select no animation. A total above 100% can leave later variants unreachable. For example, 4 / 3 / 3 is not a 40 / 30 / 30 choice; normalize it before using it for an ordinary animation mapping. The editor does not silently change imported chances or deliberate edits.

Animated props use Idle automatically. For another exported SKA, use the object's Scripted animations instructions. A map script must request it; adding an unsupported automatic action does not make a prop use that action.

docs.title: Clip and movement checks
docs.text:
Change What to do Loop seam Set Loop in Clip Settings; check the first and last poses and their curve tangents. Clip length Edit the Action's keys, then confirm Clip Settings with OK. Imported end padding is retained. Playback speed Edit clip FPS. It changes duration without moving the keys. Movement reference Set Walk / Run Reference Speed to the speed that clip was authored for. It does not set gameplay speed. Procedural look or walking limits Use the Advanced IK Tutorial.

For an in-place walk or run, the plugin cannot infer the intended travel speed from the keys. Start with a working equivalent unit's reference setting and check its motion in-game. Do not set the reference speed to zero.

Custom gameplay timings

Use Edit Events → Custom Gameplay Timings only for a deliberate timing override. Event (ms) is the trigger offset; Total (ms) includes recovery. For a hit at 500 ms in a 2000 ms sequence, enter 500 / 2000.

These values stay fixed when you change clip length or FPS. Disable the override to return to marker/phase-generated timings. Check overrides with the matching gameplay ability.

SKA text events

Advanced SKA Data on the selected animation contains text events such as <blink>. These are separate from attack/spawn markers and Effect Set events. In the engine's facial-animation path, <blink> restarts a separate eye animation when the necessary facial resources exist. It is not a general-purpose marker for ordinary Idle clips. Blender preserves these events but does not play them; practical use in Skylords needs testing.

Set automatically; keep your attention on the motion Plugin handles You choose Keyed clip range when confirming Clip Settings; scene range and FPS when pressing Play Keys, FPS, looping and interpolation Shared phase ranges and generated gameplay timings Release/phase boundaries and Actions Marker class for new ordinary attack/spawn markers; animation file CRCs Hit times and deliberate hit directions Corresponding phase weights Alternative motions and their weights Bone lookup IDs and serialized versions Bone names, rest pose and weighting Hovering timing attribute from Hovering Ground Unit Whether the model uses the hovering motion path

CRCs, versions and internal timing selectors are hidden in Artist View. Existing imported records are preserved. The plugin does not invent gameplay abilities, target behaviour, movement speed or IK chain order.

docs.title: Final check
docs.text:
Save the Animation Set and run Model Setup → Check Model. It reviews saved animation chances and clip ranges, along with mesh and material checks. Use Normalize to 100% for an ordinary mapping with a non-100 chance total. An unloaded external SKA reference is kept; load Animation Clips to preview it.

Export the intended DRS and SKAs, then reimport a copy. Check Idle and every assigned variant. Check phase transitions, hits, pushback, movement and procedural IK with the game setup in the Map Editor or game. Blender's single-clip Play button does not simulate the complete gameplay state machine.

Switching models and recovering an edit

Pending animation edits stay with their model during the current Blender session, including the selected entry. They are not saved animation data until you click Save in the editor. Save each edited model before saving your .blend or exporting it.

If saved settings changed while a draft was kept, the editor tells you. Save applies your draft; Reset loads the saved settings instead. Opening a .blend clears these session drafts and loads its saved settings.

If settings cannot be loaded, keep your source files and reimport a working model copy. Check Model identifies unreadable saved records. A failed read does not replace another model's pending draft.

docs.title: Building Guide
docs.text: Create or edit a building with intact, damaged and destroyed states. For ordinary props, use the Object Guide.

docs.title: Cells and states
docs.text:
• A cell is a building section that can be damaged separately, such as a wall section. A small building can use one cell for the whole model. A cell can contain several meshes.
  • A state is a version of that section: intact, damaged or destroyed. Choose a cell first, then the version you want to edit.

You do not need to create the state collections or work out file links by hand.

docs.title: 1. Start a building
docs.text:
Existing building: use File → Import → Battleforge Model (.drs/.bmg), then select one of its meshes. Enable collision or debris import if you intend to edit those parts.

Enable Collision Shapes and Intact-State Collision Shapes to edit intact cells' collisions too. Disable Clear Existing Content to keep existing models and Actions, including those in other scenes. Building Parts contains Construction Geometry and Debris Geometry.

New building: select your meshes, open BMG Editor → Building Editor, and click Set Up Building. This creates the intact state from your selection. Use the Object Guide for UVs and DRS materials.

For a new animated building, prepare the rig and GameOrientation using the Unit Guide, then select its meshes and click Set Up Building. Use one armature, with its object transforms applied in GameOrientation. The plugin copies the skeleton and adds an Idle starter. Assign your Idle action in Animation Set Editor.

The plugin creates GameOrientation, a 3 × 3 grid, and an Intact state in the centre cell (0, 0) containing your selected meshes. The other cells start empty. You can use this setup for a complete small building.

Duplicate creates another state from an existing one. From Selection creates the chosen cell/state assignment from your selected meshes. Export writes the state resources and their references automatically.

The plugin does not split your building into sections or sculpt damage for you. For separate damageable sections, prepare their meshes and add them to different cells with From Selection. For a damaged appearance, edit a duplicated state.

GameOrientation

Keep the building's GameOrientation unchanged. Keep imported meshes attached to their existing armature or parent. New meshes copied with From Selection keep their visible placement.

docs.title: 2. Edit a state
docs.text:
1. Open States. For a building with several parts, choose a Cell.
  2. Choose a State, then click Show.
  3. Click Select Meshes and edit normally.

Intact is state 0, Damaged is state 2, and Destroyed is state 3. Some assets also define Damage Stage 1. The picker lists the states that actually exist in the selected cell.

For ordinary building damage, prepare Intact and Damaged. The game switches to Damaged when the cell reaches its damage threshold and to Destroyed when the building is crushed. Damage Stage 1 is available for existing or special setups; adding it alone does not make the ordinary damage system switch through it. Test the building with its intended game setup.

The creation dialog offers four named states per cell. Other state IDs can exist in imported files, but we have not established a universal engine limit or automatic damage behavior for them.

To create damaged geometry, show Intact, click Duplicate, choose Damaged, and edit the copy. Its mesh data and collision shapes are independent. If no visible damage is needed, keep that Damaged copy unchanged.

For a simple building, keep using cell (0, 0): make Intact, duplicate it as Damaged, then remove or change parts of that copy. Add a Destroyed mesh only if something should remain visible, such as a ruined base.

To use different meshes, select them and click From Selection. Choose the cell coordinates and the new state. The selected meshes are copied.

Use Remove to remove the selected state from this building. Undo restores it. For multi-cell buildings, All Cells makes Show display that state in each cell that defines it. Other buildings are not changed.

docs.title: State effects
docs.text:
Click State Effects:

  • While in State: the persistent effect for this state.
  • On Entering State: the effect that plays when the building enters it.

For example, assign smoke to While in State for a damaged building, and a burst of debris to On Entering State for destruction. Leave a field blank if you do not want that assigned effect.

Enter an existing FXB or supported destruction XML reference. A destroyed state can have a transition effect without a model. No imported mesh is normal for such a state. Create or modify effect assets in the external Effect Editor.

docs.title: 3. Check the grid and collisions
docs.text:
Open Grid & Helpers:

  • Grid Overlay shows the building's cells on the ground. It is not rendered or exported.
  • Collision Shapes and Locators show or hide this building's helpers.
  • Edit Grid changes grid dimensions, spacing, rotation and building-level resources.
  • Building Size resizes the entire building, including its cells, states, collisions, attachment positions and SKA animations. 0.5 is half size; 2 is double. Export includes the resized clips automatically.

A grid radius of 0 gives 1 × 1 cells; 1 gives 3 × 3; 2 gives 5 × 5. Keep the imported settings unless you intend to change the building layout.

What the Edit Grid settings mean Setting What you use it for Resource name Name stored with this building. The export filename is chosen when exporting. Grid radius Number of cells available around the centre cell. Enlarging the grid adds empty cells; it does not split the model. Cell spacing Distance between neighbouring cells, in game units. It does not resize your meshes. Rotation Orientation of the whole building grid. Keep GameOrientation unchanged. Shared origin for all modules Enable when the sections are modeled together at one building origin. Keep the imported setting on existing assets. Ground resource Optional DRS beneath the building, such as its ground decoration. It does not create terrain. Cell hit effect Building-level hit/debris effect used when an individual cell is damaged. Building crush effect Effect for destruction of the whole building.

Cell hit effect and Building crush effect are separate from the persistent and transition effects assigned with State Effects. Blank building-level hit/crush fields allow the engine's standard building effects.

Additional cells do not make the ground walkable or create collision shapes. Place collisions separately where needed.

Edit collision shapes using the Object Guide. Use the selected state's collision collection for state-specific shapes and the building's root collision collection for building-wide shapes.

docs.title: 4. Preview damage
docs.text:
1. Open Damage Preview and click Build Preview.
  2. Drag Damage to inspect damaged geometry, scratch and destruction effects.
  3. Press Space to animate debris and FX. Use Replay to restart the transition.
  4. Use Update Preview after changing geometry, effects or terrain.
  5. Click Clear to return to editing.

The slider is a preview, not the building's exported health. Manual Show controls also leave the damage preview. After reopening a saved preview, rebuild it or clear it.

Scratch requires a scratch map with useful alpha. A white mask produces no visible darkening. Missing states are not replaced with invented geometry. Build once, then use the slider: effects are cached across the building's states. Changing Damage within the same state keeps its current effects running. Use Replay when you want to restart them.

docs.title: 5. Export
docs.text:
1. Save your working .blend.
  2. Open File → Export → BattleForge Building (.bmg) and choose a separate output folder.
  3. Keep Advanced Export Options → Model Type at Automatic (Keep Imported Setup).
  4. Keep External Resources → Local + Custom. Include animation files if you changed animations.
  5. Reimport the exported copy, then test it in the Map Editor.

Read Export Check before exporting. Fix errors such as missing materials, UVs or building states. Save pending changes in Animation Set Editor and Effect Set Editor. If an included clip is missing, load it or restore its source file. Review items do not block export.

Export includes hidden states, state DRS files, textures, local destruction XML and its meshes/ resources. Custom global dependencies go into AdditionalFiles. Review <building>.assets.json and <building>.bmg-export.json before sharing.

To edit debris, destruction XML or module resources, follow Modules, Debris & Resources.

Advanced: modular buildings and animations

Keep Shared origin enabled for sections modeled together at one building origin. Disable it for separate modules placed by the grid. Select a cell and use Cell Rotation to turn that module and all its states.

Animate the building's main armature. The plugin keeps its cells in sync; you do not need to animate the hidden cell helpers. Imported states retain their individual skeleton bindings.

Building Size leaves external FX assets at their own size. Adjust those resources in the external Effect Editor when they need different dimensions.

Advanced: standalone BMS state files

Use this for a separate state-resource module. Ordinary BMG editing uses States above and writes those links for you.

  1. Open BMG Editor → BMS Editor and choose Open BMS or New BMS.
  2. Set Resource directory to the folder containing the referenced files.
  3. For each state, enter its Resource DRS and optional FX reference. The FX runs while that state is active.
  4. Use Add State for another version. Common building IDs are 0 Intact, 2 Damaged and 3 Destroyed. Keep the imported IDs for other modules.
  5. For an effect when a state begins, use Add Transition and enter its destination State ID and FX reference.
  6. Use Check State Resources. Import DRS Preview opens a referenced model for editing; export that DRS separately after changing it.
  7. Open File → Export → BattleForge Mesh States (.bms) and keep the referenced DRS and FX assets available.

Leave Advanced File Settings unchanged for an existing module. A BMS does not pack the models or effects into one file. Local resource checks need loose files; engine-resolved assets in archives may still be available in the game. Check the final module and FX in the Map Editor.

Advanced: construction and debris

BMS files describe state resources; they do not contain mesh geometry. Use BMG Editor → BMS Editor for standalone BMS references. Construction and destruction XML/FX graphs are separate assets and need their own editor.

Blender previews use cached debris physics and bounded particles. Exact engine collision/inertia, gameplay impulses, spatial audio and all shader effects are not reproduced. Test the final result in the Map Editor.

For materials and animation events, see the Material Guide and Effects Guide.

docs.title: Advanced Effects Tutorial
docs.text: Time existing sounds and effects, attach continuous effects, and check their preview. Create the FX resources themselves in the external Effect Editor. Start with the Effect Set Guide if your library is not set up.

docs.title: Time a sound and a visual together
docs.text:
Example: an attack should play an impact sound and a burst at 30% of its Action.

  1. Play that Action in Animation Set Editor, then pause at the impact pose.
  2. Open Effect Set Editor and add an animation entry. It selects the Action currently assigned to the model's armature.
  3. Add an event. Choose Sound, then use the clock button beside Time (Use Playhead on hover).
  4. Open Effect Selector, choose the sound and keep its Chance at 100%.
  5. Add another event, choose World FX, set Time to the same value and select the visual resource at Chance 100%.
  6. Click Update Preview, enable Sound and press Space.
  7. Adjust placement and volume, then click Save.

Two events play two layers. Two variants in one event choose between them. Use a separate Sound event for each simultaneous sound layer too.

Use Playhead reads a fraction of the whole Action, including its stored end padding. Play the selected Action on the model first; a different active Action cannot supply its time. The event can be at 0.3 even when the current Blender frame is not frame 30.

If an attack uses a hit marker, set the FX event to that marker's Time. A marker does not create a sound or visual event automatically.

docs.title: Choose World FX, Linked FX or a locator
docs.text:
Wanted result Use Burst at an animation moment, placed with Offset World FX event Existing FX with its own source/target or controller setup Linked FX event Fire attached continuously to a hand, weapon or body Persistent FX locator Destruction tied to a building's damage state Building Editor → Damage Preview

For a hand flame, open Locator Editor, add a Persistent Figure FX locator, attach it to the intended bone, choose the effect and save placement. Follow the Locator Guide.

An event's Offset is not a bone attachment. Do not keep nudging an unattached World FX event to make it follow an animated hand.

docs.title: Fade an attached effect during an Action
docs.text:
Example: a persistent hand flame should fade out halfway through a clip and return near its end.

  1. Set up and preview the persistent locator first.
  2. In that Action's EffectSet entry, add Fade Out Persistent FX at Time 0.5.
  3. Use the same effect filename as the persistent locator.
  4. Set Fade Duration (s), for example 0.2.
  5. Add Fade In Persistent FX at Time 0.9, using the same resource name.
  6. Update the preview, play the clip and save.

Fade events affect an effect that already exists. They do not spawn a new one. If a fade has no effect, compare the event and locator filenames first.

docs.title: Alternatives, occasional sounds and silence
docs.text:
Event variants Result 40 / 30 / 30 Always one of three resources 80 / 20 Always one of two resources One variant at 25 A resource on 25% of choices; otherwise silence/no FX 4 / 3 / 3 90% chance of silence/no FX

Click Normalize to 100% when you want to keep the proportions but always choose a resource. This changes the saved chances; it is not a preview setting. Avoid totals above 100%.

Use Selected Variant while checking each sound or visual. Switch back to Engine Chances to preview the saved choices. A single event's random choice does not have to match a live game's random sequence.

docs.title: Sound variation and game playback
docs.text:
Keep Volume and Pitch Min / Max in the event's main controls. For a small pitch variation, use −0.05 / 0.05. Zero leaves playback rate unchanged; pitch changes also change duration. Keep the playback rate positive.

Open Game Playback for the settings that require an in-game check:

  • Min / Max Falloff: the sound's distance settings. Blender timeline audio does not reproduce positional attenuation. Keep a working imported range until you can test it in-game.
  • Interruptible: controls handling when an animation is interrupted. An uninterrupted Blender timeline cannot demonstrate that case.

The stored Condition is retained in Debug View. The inspected animation-event path does not use it for filtering; leave it unchanged.

docs.title: Preview and edit efficiently
docs.text:
1. Build once with Update Preview.
  2. Keep Live Update enabled while adjusting event time, variants, volume, pitch or offset. Changes rebuild after a short pause.
  3. Press Space for the shared timeline; flow and FX do not need separate clocks.
  4. Rebuild after changing the model's motion, terrain contacts or external resources.
  5. Turn Effects off to return to plain model animation, or Sound off for a silent FX preview. Turning Effects on reuses the cached preview. Use × beside Update Preview to remove the generated FX and audio completely.

For effects touching the floor, place a terrain mesh outside the model's export collection before rebuilding. Without a terrain mesh, the preview uses flat ground.

Add Render Setup → Add Render and use F12 to inspect supported refraction and glow. Check the effect from several angles. Transparent particle sorting, heat haze, scene fog and some gameplay links still need the Map Editor or game.

Effects with their own animation controller

Keep the referenced DRS, SKA, meshes and textures available in the library. The preview loads supported controllers automatically; you do not need to create another armature or assign the effect's Action to the unit.

If an effect is misplaced or incomplete, read Effect Preview Report in Blender's Text Editor. Check missing dependencies and attachment targets before changing the unit's animation. Do not edit generated preview meshes.

Automatic preview setup

The plugin resolves installed resources, shares loaded assets, builds supported geometry/materials and applies the effect's animation tracks. Billboard masks, texture-atlas animation and supported UV offset/zoom come from the resource; no extra switch is required in the model's EffectSet.

These previews are generated helpers and are excluded from model exports. Gameplay interruption, spatial audio and unavailable target links still need an engine check. A missing dependency is not replaced with a matching-looking effect.

docs.title: Share the result
docs.text:
Save the EffectSet and .blend, export the model and its intended SKAs, and include custom external FX plus their dependencies separately. Reimport a copy and check both the selected variants and the saved chance settings in-game.

Before exporting, run Model Setup → Check Model after saving the editors. It flags empty resources, invalid event values and totals above 100%. A valid chance of silence below 100% is kept and is not reported as a mistake.

docs.title: Modules, debris and external resources
docs.text: Use this guide when a model needs more than its main DRS or BMG: modules, damage-state meshes, destruction XML, effects, textures or sounds.

docs.title: 1. Find the model's files
docs.text:
1. Select your model.
  2. Open External Resources in DRS Editor. For a building, open it inside BMG Editor → Building Editor.
  3. Click Find Resources.
  4. Use Show to choose models, effects, textures or audio.

Select a file to see its Source File and available editing tools. Refresh checks the references again after you change a locator or effect.

docs.title: 2. Edit destruction settings
docs.text:
For a building, choose a damaged or destroyed state and click Edit Destruction. You can also select its XML in External Resources and click Destruction XML.

  1. Select Destruction Settings to change the duration.
  2. Select a Debris entry to change its name or model filename.
  3. Select its Priority entry to change which pieces take priority when the game limits debris. Priority does not change the piece's mass.
  4. Select a curve or key to change its timing and values.
  5. Click OK, then save your .blend.

Changes stay in the .blend and are included on export. The source XML stays unchanged.

Control Use Duration How long the effect or selected curve runs, in seconds. Time (0–1) Position within that curve: 0 is its start, 1 is its end. Ground Level Debris collision-plane height. Lower it near the end to let pieces sink away. Alpha Fade: 0 is invisible, 1 is fully visible. Add Debris Add a piece, then enter the DRS filename it should use. Add Key / Remove Add a curve key, or remove the selected key or piece.

Use Build Preview or Update Preview in Damage Preview to see the saved changes. Space plays the preview.

Advanced: curves and other XML fields

Each curve has its own duration. Changing the effect duration does not rescale its curves. Select the curve itself to edit its duration and addressing mode.

Advanced Fields reveals attachment settings and other stored XML fields. Existing fields and comments are retained. Some native XML settings have no Blender preview; test their exported result in the Map Editor.

docs.title: 3. Edit a debris or module model
docs.text:
1. Select its DRS in External Resources.
  2. Click Edit Resource Model.
  3. Edit the imported mesh, materials or collision as usual.
  4. Select the main model again before exporting it.

The edited resource is included with its owner. If you imported a building with Debris enabled in this version, edits to those imported debris meshes are also included. For an older .blend, reimport the debris or use Edit Resource Model.

For a module BMS, click Edit Mesh States. Make the changes in BMG Editor → BMS Editor. They are included when you export the main model.

Use Edit Resource Model for module geometry or animation edits. Locator module previews are for placement; the export check stops if those preview meshes were changed, so their edits cannot be silently lost.

docs.title: 4. Use your own effect or file
docs.text:
1. Give the new resource a unique filename in your working folder.
  2. Set that filename in the model's Locator, Effect Set or State Effects settings.
  3. Click + in External Resources.
  4. Enter the same Referenced Filename and choose its Working File.

To replace a file already listed, change its Source File to your working copy. Refresh the effect or damage preview after changing resources.

Use unique filenames to keep the original effect available. Replacing an existing global filename affects every model that uses that filename after installation.

Advanced: effect editing and shared resources

Create or edit FXB effects in the Effect Editor, then bind the resulting file here. For sound sets, keep every audio variant and any SNR/SNS pair together. Use game-ready resources; this exporter does not convert source WAVs to the game's audio format.

Multiple locators can share one module. Editing its resource changes all uses of that file. To give one locator a different version, use a separate filename and update that locator's reference.

docs.title: 5. Export the package
docs.text:
1. Open File → Export → BattleForge Model (.drs) or BattleForge Building (.bmg).
  2. Keep External Resources → Local + Custom.
  3. Choose a separate export folder and export.
  4. Review <model>.assets.json for files that were not found or were left as installed-game references.

Standalone BattleForge Mesh States (.bms) exports offer the same resource choices and include their referenced state models and destruction files.

Everything is written inside the export folder you chose. It can contain:

Text Only
my_building.bmg
my_building_cell…drs
animation.ska
destruction.xml
textures.dds
meshes/
    debris_piece.drs
AdditionalFiles/
    INSTALL.txt
    bf1/gfx/effects/…
    bf1/sound/…
my_building.assets.json

Keep the main model, module files, XML, textures and meshes/ together in a dedicated model folder. Point the object's game resource entry at that model. For a new copy of an existing model, use a new model folder to keep its local XML and debris separate from the original.

docs.title: Open the exported model in Blender
docs.text:
Keep AdditionalFiles beside the main .drs, .bmg or .bms, then import that main file. Blender uses the packaged resources first and the configured Skylords installation for anything the package does not include. If neither contains a resource, the error names the missing file.

You can move or share the whole export folder. You do not need to install its files in the game to import or preview it in Blender.

docs.title: Install for a game test
docs.text:
Keep the model's local files together in their dedicated model folder. Install the files in AdditionalFiles using your project's game asset workflow, preserving their bf1/... paths. Then test the complete package in the Map Editor.

Advanced: export choices

Local + Custom includes local module/state/destruction resources and custom or edited global dependencies. Unchanged global game assets remain references. Include Original on a resource also packages that original.

All References also copies unchanged global dependencies. It can create a much larger package. Model Files Only skips dependency packaging.

Main-model clips follow Include Animation Files. Referenced module and custom-effect controllers retain the animation files they need.

Detection uses the configured Skylords folder, working-file bindings and recorded file fingerprints. An original modified before its first scan cannot be identified as an edit automatically; bind a working copy or include it explicitly. Unrecognized or missing dependencies are listed in the manifest.

docs.title: Advanced IK Tutorial
docs.text:
Edit the limits used by the game's procedural IK, or bake a Blender IK rig into an ordinary animation. These are two different workflows.

Your goal Workflow Adjust a working unit's procedural look/walking limits Edit IK Limits below. Animate with Blender controllers and export the resulting motion Bake onto the deform rig.

docs.title: Adjust an imported IK bone
docs.text:
Use an existing unit with a working IK setup for your first edit.

  1. Select the model's deform armature and enter Pose Mode.
  2. Select a bone with imported IK data.
  3. Open Animation Set Editor → IK Limits.
  4. Click Edit Angle Limits if the angle controls are not present yet.
  5. Edit Min / Max for an enabled axis. For a small test, tighten one existing range slightly rather than changing every bone.
  6. Keep the bone's purpose and chain settings, export the DRS and check the procedural response with the matching unit in-game.

Select X, Y or Z to enable or disable a limit axis. Only enabled axes show their angle controls. Disabling an axis does not erase its stored values. Keep the imported rest pose and bone orientation while comparing changes.

Normal playback does not demonstrate game IK

The game supplies procedural targets and movement state. These limits do not create a look target or a foot-placement solver in Blender. The generated Limit Rotation constraint stays muted so your keyed Action is not altered. Use ordinary playback to check the base animation, and an engine test to check the procedural response.

docs.title: Choose which IK setup uses the bone
docs.text:
Look At and Curve Walking select the engine IK purposes for this bone. A bone can belong to either or both. Keep the purposes from a working equivalent model unless you are rebuilding its procedural setup.

In each Action variant, leave Allows IK enabled when the game should apply its procedural IK during that animation. Disabling it for a clip does not remove the bone's limits from the model.

docs.title: Advanced IK Settings
docs.text:
Expand Advanced IK Settings for chain order, inversion and damping.

Setting What to edit Chain Order Preserve the imported order. Bone parenting alone is not enough to generate the intended engine chain order. Inverted Preserve this engine purpose flag unless you are deliberately rebuilding the IK setup. Start Min / Max Damping-start angles for that enabled axis. Keep them consistent with the working bone's angle limits. Motion Retained How much rotation beyond the damping start remains: 1 keeps it; 0 stops at the start angle. Hard Min / Max limits still apply.

Example: with Start Max 20°, an attempted rotation of 40° becomes 20° at 0, 30° at 0.5, or 40° at 1, before the hard limits are applied. Lower Motion Retained values give stronger damping. A pose inside the damping-start range is unaffected by this step.

Change one setting at a time and compare in the engine. The Blender constraint does not reproduce the game's complete damping solver. There is no automatic chain rebuild or procedural-IK preview to validate a new setup for you.

docs.title: Add or remove an IK entry
docs.text:
For a bone without imported IK, click Add IK Limits. Choose its purposes and axes, then adjust its limits. New entries start with the plugin's basic defaults; they are not a finished procedural rig. Use a working equivalent model as a reference for the chain setup and test the new model in-game.

Remove IK Limits removes only that bone's exported IK entry and the plugin's limit helper. Its animation keys and other bones' entries remain intact.

Bone lookup IDs and supported record versions are written automatically. You do not need to type a bone index or calculate a flag mask. Hidden imported axes, unknown purpose bits and other untouched data are retained.

docs.title: Bake Blender IK into a SKA
docs.text:
Use this when the desired motion comes from a Blender IK constraint or control rig.

  1. Keep an editable copy of your original rig and Action.
  2. Bake the evaluated Pose motion onto the model's deform armature with Visual Keying enabled. Include every deform bone that needs motion.
  3. On the export copy, mute the controls/constraints that would apply that motion a second time. Play the baked Action to check the result.
  4. Check that the deform bones have quaternion rotation curves. SKA exports translation and rotation. For a whole-model size change, use Model Setup → Model Size; it updates the skeleton and animation translations. Redesign animated bone scaling as translation/rotation motion for a SKA export.
  5. Assign the baked Action in Animation Set Editor, confirm Clip Settings and save the animation set.
  6. Export the DRS and SKA together, then reimport a copy and compare the motion.

Do not change the rest pose after baking without updating the model and its animations together. An imported control rig is not a replacement for the export deform skeleton.

Which parts are automatic?

The plugin handles bone lookup mapping, serialization and preservation of untouched IK data. You choose the intended pose limits, purposes, chain setup and any Blender bake. Game targets and gameplay behaviour cannot be derived from an Action's keys.

Return to the Advanced Animation Tutorial for phase timing, hit markers and final animation checks.

docs.title: Default Material Guide
docs.text: Use this guide to set up Default materials in Blender 5. For cutouts, smooth transparency and flowing surfaces, see the Shading Recipes.

docs.title: 1. Open the Material Editor
docs.text:
1. Select the part of your model you want to edit.
  2. In the 3D Viewport, press N and open DRS Editor > Material Editor.
  3. If needed, click Create DRS Material or Create / Upgrade DRS Material.
  4. Set Material Type to Default. Stay in Artist View.

An imported model usually already has its material. Upgrading an older setup creates a new material and keeps the old one. Check the textures afterward.

docs.title: 2. Add your textures
docs.text:
Open Textures. Assign each image to its matching slot and tick the box beside it to include it. You do not need to connect shader nodes or change image settings.

Slot What to put here ColorMap The model's color texture, usually named _col. Start here. NormalMap Surface detail such as cracks and bumps, usually _nor. ParamMap A packed texture controlling surface properties, usually _par. FluidMap The moving color layer for effects such as lava, usually _flu. EnvironmentMap A reflection cubemap. Optional; see reflections below. RefractionParamMap A distortion texture for the view behind the model. Optional. DistortionParamMap A separate distortion effect driven by the map's alpha gradients. Optional. ScratchMap A texture whose alpha controls the scratch darkening effect. Optional.

Leave unused maps disabled. For imported models, keep the original slot assignments; filenames alone do not decide how the game uses a texture.

Enable Auto map flags to keep the normal and parameter-map switches in sync with your assigned maps. Calculate Map Flags updates them once instead. Neither button chooses transparency or reflection settings for you.

docs.title: Choose where surface values come from
docs.text:
Use Parameter Source in Textures:

Choice Use it when… Packed _par / _spec You already have a packed parameter texture. For Default, assign it to ParamMap. Separate artist maps You have separate roughness, metalness, mask and emission images. The plugin packs them on export. Use matching image sizes. Scalar values You want one value across the whole mesh. Edit the sliders in Material Parameters.

For a Default parameter texture, the channels are:

Channel Controls Red Smoothness: higher values make smoother highlights. Green Metalness: higher values make the surface more metallic. Blue The flow mask. In reflection variants it also controls reflection contribution. Alpha Emissivity: the surface's glow contribution. This is not transparency.

In Separate artist maps mode, roughness is converted to smoothness automatically. Use grayscale images; the plugin reads each image's red channel. Missing separate maps fall back to the packed map, or zero if none is assigned.

Why did the sliders disappear? A parameter map replaces Smoothness, Metalness, Reflectivity and Emissivity. Edit the map instead. Choose Scalar values if you want to use those sliders.

docs.title: Paint a texture
docs.text:
Click Paint beside the texture slot you want to edit. The plugin creates an editable, packed working image, keeps any existing strokes, and selects it for both image and model painting. Original game files stay unchanged. Reusing Paint continues on the same working image. Edited textures are converted back to DDS when you export the model.

Some compressed DDS images can show painted pixels in the Image Editor while the model still displays old GPU texture data. Paint avoids that path by using an uncompressed working image. After painting, save your image to a separate PNG with Image > Save As, and save your .blend file.

Imported UVs may sit a whole tile below the base image. This comes from the V-axis conversion and looks the same with Repeat sampling. Paint shows one image and leaves the UVs unchanged. UVs below the base tile can remain outside the visible image; this does not change Repeat sampling on the model. Shared or overlapping UVs make a brush stroke appear on every mesh part using those pixels. For unique painting on each part, give it unique UV space and texture content first.

docs.title: 3. Enable the features you need
docs.text:
Open Material Flags. Leave imported flags alone unless you are changing that feature.

Setting When to use it UseParameterMap Use the packed or separate parameter maps. Auto map flags can handle this. UseNormalMap Use your NormalMap. Auto map flags can handle this. EnableAlphaTest Cut holes in a surface, such as the spaces between leaves. Pixels below the alpha cutoff are discarded. This does not enable smooth, glass-like transparency. UseEnvironmentMap Add reflections from a cubemap. DecalMode Use the game's decal rendering path. Leave it off for ordinary solid models.

For cutouts, put the opacity mask in ColorMap alpha. Keep ParamMap alpha for emissivity. The game's final transparency also depends on its rendering setup; check the edges in the Map Editor.

docs.title: 4. Adjust the appearance
docs.text:
Open Material Parameters and enable the values you want to export. Only controls relevant to your setup appear in Artist View. Where a parameter has a defined range, its control limits the value automatically.

  • Saturation: lower it to reduce color intensity.
  • SpecularScale (approx.): adjusts highlight strength. Blender previews an approximation, so check the final result in the Map Editor.
  • Scratch: controls darkening from ScratchMap alpha. It needs a ScratchMap.
  • Distortion Mesh Scale (approx.): moves the distortion effect away from the surface. Assign a DistortionParamMap to show this control.
  • Smoothness, Metalness, Reflectivity, Emissivity: available in Scalar values mode. With maps enabled, edit the corresponding map channels instead.

docs.title: Moving textures: flow
docs.text:
Assign FluidMap and a parameter map with a blue flow mask. Blue marks where the fluid layer blends into the base color. Press Space to play the timeline; the mesh itself does not have to move.

To adjust the movement, open Flow — Speed and Direction and enable Custom Flow Settings:

  • Minimum Speed / Maximum Speed: the direction and speed range on each axis. Use the same minimum and maximum for steady movement.
  • Speed Variation: how the speed changes within that range.
  • Pattern Scale: the size of the flow pattern.

Leave Custom Flow Settings off to use the engine defaults. This does not disable flow.

docs.title: Bending in the wind
docs.text: In Material Parameters, enable WindResponse and WindHeight. Start with a small WindResponse within 0–0.1; zero means no movement. WindHeight (0–10) sets where bending begins along the model's game height axis. Increase it to keep more of the base still. The plugin adds the preview automatically. Press Space to see it. During Texture Paint, wind deformation is paused to keep the surface stable; it returns when you leave paint mode. Exported wind values are unchanged.

docs.title: Reflections and refraction
docs.text:
For reflections, enable UseEnvironmentMap. Assign an EnvironmentMap in Textures, or use Use Bundled Environment when that helper is shown. The game can use a fallback environment when no map is assigned.

For refraction, assign RefractionParamMap, then adjust RefractionScale and RefractionColor. The preview is set up automatically. Refraction distorts the view behind the surface; it is separate from reflections and alpha cutouts. Blender approximates this effect and does not reproduce the game's refraction blur. See refraction details only if you need to author the texture channels yourself.

docs.title: 5. Check the whole model
docs.text:
1. Open DRS Editor → Render Setup.
  2. Keep Environment: Forge, then click Add Render.
  3. Switch to Rendered shading. Press Space for flow and wind.
