The camera frames the whole model in your current scene. Forge uses the installed Forge's sunlight, sky/ground light colors and terrain texture. Enable Forge Props to add a crystal behind the model, then click Update Render. The render collection is excluded from export.

Sun Rays adds soft, Forge-textured shafts with an animated cloud mask. Toggle it, then click Update Render. Press Space to animate the mask. Rays are enabled by default in Forge mode and do not affect exported models.

Set Skylords Reborn Folder in the add-on preferences to load Forge resources. If they are unavailable, the preview uses Studio lighting and tells you.

Exposure in Render Setup adjusts overall brightness. The default is 0; 1 makes the whole image twice as bright, including glowing textures. It does not add a missing light. For stronger directional light, adjust the Sun's Energy in Blender's Light Data Properties.

Blender render using Forge resources. Check the final result in the Map Editor; Blender's shaders, ambient lighting and post-processing can differ from the game.

Export a test, import it again, and check it in the Map Editor before sharing it.

docs.title: If something looks wrong
docs.text:
Problem Check first No material controls Select a mesh with an active DRS material. Texture has no effect Check the slot checkbox and its matching material flag. Smoothness or metalness sliders have no effect The parameter map may be supplying those values instead. Flow or wind is still Play the timeline with Space. Check the map or WindResponse. Rendered view is dark Use Add Render to add lighting. Blender and game look different Compare in the Map Editor; lighting, reflections and refraction have preview limits.

Use the Shading Recipes for smooth transparency and the limits of other material types.

docs.title: Artist Model Pipeline
docs.text: Choose a guide for your model, then export and check a copy in the Map Editor. Save your editable work as a .blend and use a separate export folder.

docs.title: Choose your model
docs.text:
You are making Follow A static or animated prop Object Guide A rigged unit Unit Guide A building with damage states Building Guide

Each guide covers editing an imported model and starting a new one. You do not need a separate Blender startup scene or an old material library. Use Set Up Model for a new DRS model or Set Up Building for a new BMG.

docs.title: Model and material
docs.text:
1. Prepare your meshes and UVs.
  2. Select a mesh and open DRS Editor → Material Editor.
  3. Create its DRS material, choose the material type and assign textures.
  4. Add collision shapes if your model needs them.
  5. Run Model Setup → Check Model and fix its errors.

Use the Default Material Guide for texture painting, cutouts, flow, wind and reflections. Use the Shading Recipes for smooth transparency and refraction.

For a whole-model preview, click DRS Editor → Render Setup → Add Render. It adds lights, a camera and ground in your current scene. Switch to Rendered shading; press Space for animated flow and wind. Keep Environment: Forge for the installed Forge's lighting and paving. Forge Props adds an optional crystal; Update Render applies setup changes.

docs.title: Animate and attach effects
docs.text:
Skip this section for static models without effects.

Task Where to do it Assign Idle, movement and attack Actions Animation Set Editor Set clip duration, FPS and looping Animation Set Editor → Clip Settings → Edit Settings Set a release or spawn moment Animation Set Editor → Edit Markers Place a health bar, projectile point or persistent effect Locator Editor Schedule a sound or effect during an animation Effect Set Editor Create damaged states and preview destruction Building Editor

For worked examples, use the Advanced Animation, Advanced Effects and Advanced IK tutorials. They cover phase clips, hit timing, sound/FX layers and procedural limits.

Click Save after editing AnimationSet or EffectSet. After moving a locator, click Save Placement. Save the .blend too.

Animation and effect drafts stay with their model while you switch models in this session. Save each edited model's settings before exporting or saving the .blend. Check Model reviews those saved settings, including animation chances and effect events; it keeps intentional FX silence unchanged.

To resize a DRS model, use Model Setup → Model Size. For a complete building, use Building Editor → Grid & Helpers → Building Size. These controls include the model's animations and attachments; external effects retain their own size.

docs.title: Export and check
docs.text:
1. Save your editor changes and .blend.
  2. For DRS, use File → Export → BattleForge Model (.drs) and choose the correct model type. Include referenced SKA Actions when exporting animations.
  3. For BMG, use File → Export → BattleForge Building (.bmg). Keep External Resources → Local + Custom to include modules, debris, destruction XML and your custom global resources.
  4. Fix errors listed in Export Check. Expand its review items when needed. Save pending Animation Set and Effect Set edits; restore missing included clips.
  5. Reimport the exported copy into a new scene and inspect it.
  6. Check the final model, animations, collision and effects in the Map Editor.

For models with animations, play the whole clip and check its loop. For buildings, check every state. Keep packaged custom effects and sounds with their dependencies; unchanged global game assets remain references. See Modules, Debris & Resources for editing and installation.

Standalone BMS state resources

Open BMG Editor → BMS Editor to create or edit a standalone BMS. A BMS references state models and effects; it does not contain their geometry.

Set Resource directory, use Check State Resources, then export a BMS copy. Export edited DRS state models separately and keep the referenced effects available. Use the Building Guide for the complete BMG workflow.

Advanced data and preview limits

Use Artist View for normal authoring. Debug View exposes imported technical fields when a specific repair needs them.

Advanced SKA Data contains text events and target IDs whose authoring workflow is not fully established. Keep imported values unless deliberately testing them. Blender does not execute those game events.

Bake control-rig, constraint and NLA motion onto deform bones before export. Check the exported SKA by importing it again.

The individual guides explain preview limits and where to use the external Effect Editor or Map Editor. Final gameplay and engine-dependent shading still need the game tools.

docs.title: Object Guide: from Blender to DRS
docs.text: Create and export static or animated props, such as rocks, gates and moving machinery.

docs.title: A. Edit an existing DRS
docs.text:
1. Put the .drs, its textures and any referenced .ska clips in the same folder.
  2. Choose File → Import → Battleforge Model (.drs/.bmg) and open the .drs.
  3. Select the visible model mesh and make your changes.

Disable Clear Existing Content in the import options to keep objects already in the file, including other scenes. Animation Clips loads the model's referenced animations.

Continue at step 3. Skip Set Up Model.

docs.title: B. Make a model from scratch
docs.text: Create your model in Blender. Select its meshes, then follow step 2.

docs.title: C. Use a model from another program
docs.text:
Import the model with Blender. Select its meshes, then follow step 2.

Using a rigged model as a static object

Duplicate the meshes and convert the copies to meshes in the desired pose. Continue with these copies.

docs.title: 2. Set up a new model
docs.text:
Skip this step for an imported DRS.

  1. Select your model meshes.
  2. Open DRS Editor → Model Setup → Set Up Model.
  3. Choose Static Object or Animated Object, enter a name such as object_stone_block, and keep Include Selected Meshes enabled.
  4. Enable Collision Support if your object needs collision; otherwise leave it off. Click OK.

GameOrientation — your model's parent object

GameOrientation converts between Blender and game coordinates. Import and Set Up Model create it for you.

  • Move, rotate and resize your meshes. Leave GameOrientation unchanged.
  • Keep visible meshes in Meshes_Collection. For a static object, parent them to GameOrientation.
  • For an animated object, parent the deform armature to GameOrientation and keep skinned meshes attached to their armature.
  • Moving a mesh into the collection does not parent it.
  • Parenting without preserving transforms can rotate or mirror a mesh. Use Object (Keep Transform) to keep its current placement.
Advanced: add another mesh

Move the new mesh into this model's Meshes_Collection and parent it to GameOrientation using Object (Keep Transform).

Use the GameOrientation from the same model. Keep existing rigged meshes attached to their armature.

docs.title: Resize the whole model
docs.text:
Select a model mesh and change DRS Editor → Model Setup → Model Size. 1 is the original size, 0.5 is half size and 2 is double size. This also works for animated DRS objects and units. No changes to keyframes or bone sizes are needed. Set it back to 1 to restore the original size.

Export normally. The plugin includes appropriately sized animation files, even for clips you did not load into Blender. Collision shapes and attachment positions follow the model. External effect files keep their own size. Save the .blend to keep the editable size setting.

For an entire BMG building, use Building Editor → Grid & Helpers → Building Size.

docs.title: 3. Check your model
docs.text:
• Use UV-mapped meshes. Apply modeling modifiers such as Mirror and Subdivision on an export copy; keep Armature and the plugin's wind preview modifier.
  • Use one DRS material per mesh. Separate multi-material meshes by material.
  • Check size and facing against an imported game object if you have one available.

Click Model Setup → Check Model. Select a message and click Select Object to find the mesh that needs attention. Fix errors, then run the check again.

Already imported a DRS and only changed its shape? Keep its existing material and go to step 6.

Advanced: large models and export errors
  • Keep each mesh and the combined model below 32,767 exported vertices. Leave room for extra vertices at UV seams.
  • If you reach the limit, reduce the geometry or export smaller, separate DRS objects.
  • Apply geometry modifiers on a copy before exporting. Keep the editable original.
  • If export fails, read the add-on log and fix the reported object first.

docs.title: 4. Create a DRS material
docs.text: Select a mesh and open DRS Editor → Material Editor. Click Create DRS Material, or Create / Upgrade DRS Material for a mesh that already has a material. Choose Default as the material type and keep Artist View.

docs.title: 5. Load your textures
docs.text:
1. Open Textures.
  2. Click the folder icon beside ColorMap and choose your PNG or DDS color texture.
  3. If you have a normal map, load it into NormalMap.
  4. Leave Auto map flags enabled.

For an imported DRS, keep the assigned textures or replace the ones you want to change. For a foreign model, load its textures here.

Check the result in Material Preview. For a lit preview, use DRS Editor → Render Setup → Add Render. Keep Environment: Forge to use the installed Forge's lighting and ground. Forge Props is optional. Click Update Render after changing the setup. Sun Rays adds the Forge light shafts; press Space to animate their cloud mask.

For cut-out leaves or fences, enable EnableAlphaTest under Material Flags. See the Default Material Guide for more material options.

docs.title: 6. Add collision shapes
docs.text:
Skip this step if your object does not need collision.

If you did not enable Collision Support during setup, create CollisionShapes_Collection inside your model, with Boxes_Collection, Spheres_Collection and Cylinders_Collection inside it.

  1. Add cubes, spheres or cylinders and fit them around your model. Use several shapes if needed.
  2. Move cubes into Boxes_Collection, spheres into Spheres_Collection, and cylinders into Cylinders_Collection under this model's CollisionShapes_Collection.
  3. Parent the shapes to GameOrientation using Object (Keep Transform).
  4. Set them to Wire display and disable rendering for these helper objects.

Keep boxes rectangular, spheres round and cylinders circular. Avoid bevels and shear.

docs.title: 7. Animate your object
docs.text: For a static object, continue to export.

docs.title: Prepare the rig
docs.text:
For an imported animated DRS, keep its existing rig. For a new rig:

  1. Put the deform armature in Armature_Collection, directly under your DRSModel_… collection. Create that collection if it is missing.
  2. Before weighting or animating, parent the new armature to GameOrientation using Object (Without Inverse). Set its local location and rotation to 0, and scale to 1.
  3. Rig and weight your meshes. Keep them in Meshes_Collection, parented to the armature using Object (Keep Transform).
  4. Check that each mesh's Armature modifier points to that rig. Use no more than four bone weights per vertex. Run Animation Set Editor → Skinning → Check Skin Weights.

Use Quaternion (WXYZ) rotation on deform bones before animating. SKA stores bone location and quaternion rotation; animated bone scale is not exported. Animate the deform bones, keeping the armature object and GameOrientation still.

docs.title: Assign the Idle animation
docs.text:
1. Create your repeating motion as an Action on the deform armature.
  2. Select a model mesh and open DRS Editor → Animation Set Editor.
  3. Click Initialize Animation Set (or Init), choose Animated Object, leave Replace Existing Mappings off and confirm.
  4. Select Idle in Base mode and assign your Action to its variant, or keep the imported Action.
  5. Open Clip Settings → Edit Settings. Set the clip timing and Time addressing → Loop, then confirm with OK.
  6. Use Play to check the loop, then click Save in Animation Set Editor.

Animated objects automatically play Base Idle. Other action types are greyed out.

Advanced: rig controls and IK

Bake the evaluated motion onto the deform bones of an export copy. Export keyed bone location and quaternion rotation. Keep the original control rig. Check the exported SKA after reimport.

Advanced: a rig from another program

Use a compatible imported DRS rig or prepare a new rig as above. Transfer the mesh and retarget the animation to that deform rig. Bake control-rig motion onto the deform bones of an export copy, then check a DRS/SKA reimport. Keep your original foreign rig intact.

Advanced: play another animation from a map script

Gate setup:

  • Decorative gate: keep the frame and door in one model.
  • Gate that opens a passage: export the frame and door as separate models, each with its own collision shape. Place them separately in the map.

To control the door:

  1. Create the opening motion as a separate Action.
  2. Select a model mesh or its rig, then use File → Export → BattleForge Animation (.ska). Choose the opening Action under Animation and export it.
  3. Give the SKA filename to the map author. Their script plays it on the door and switches the door's blocking when opening or closing the passage.

Keep Idle in AnimationSet. Do not add an Attack or Walk mapping for this clip.

docs.title: 8. Export
docs.text:
1. Select a mesh belonging to the model.
  2. Open File → Export → BattleForge Model (.drs).
  3. Choose a separate output folder and a filename such as object_stone_block.drs.

  4. Choose the matching Model Type:

    Object Without collision With collision Static Static Object (no collision) Static Object (with collision) Animated Animated Object (no collision) Animated Object (with collision)

  5. For an animated object, enable Include Animation Files to include the clips assigned in your saved AnimationSet. Keep No Prefix unless you need a different naming scheme.

  6. Keep the other defaults and click Export DRS. Advanced Export Options contains texture mipmaps and mesh preparation settings.

Check Export Check in the export window. Fix any errors before exporting: assign a DRS material, add missing UVs, or choose a Model Type that matches your skeleton and collision shapes. Items marked for review do not block export.

Keep External Resources → Local + Custom if the object uses modules or custom effects. See Modules, Debris & Resources to edit and package those files.

For animated objects, save pending changes in Animation Set Editor and Effect Set Editor first. If an included animation file is missing, load the clip or restore its source file. You can review the full report with Model Setup → Check Model after the export check.

Advanced: export options

For extra mesh controls, open Advanced Export Options in the export window.

Option Setting Split UV Seams Keep enabled unless you have prepared the splits yourself. Flip Face Normals Use only to correct confirmed inside-out faces. Triangulate Faces Keep enabled to export quads as triangles. Texture Mipmaps Keep Full Chain. Change only to limit the exported mip levels. Debug Export → Keep Export Copy Enable to inspect the prepared export copy.

Texture Mipmaps controls which image levels are saved in the DDS. It does not force the game to choose a sharper level at a given distance.

docs.title: 9. Check the exported copy
docs.text:
1. Keep the exported .drs, .dds textures and any .ska clips together in the output folder.
  2. Import the DRS into a fresh Blender scene. Enable Collision Shapes if used. Check orientation, size, textures and collision fit. For an animated object, also enable Animation Clips and check the full Idle loop.
  3. Test it in the Skylords Map Editor.

If a texture is missing, check its slot in Material Editor and the export folder.

docs.title: Unit Guide
docs.text:
For detailed animation, effect and IK workflows, use the Advanced Animation, Advanced Effects and Advanced IK tutorials.

Create or edit a rigged unit and export its model, textures and animations. For props, use the Object Guide. For buildings with damage states, use the Building Guide.

docs.title: 1. Choose your starting point
docs.text:
Existing unitNew unitForeign model
  1. Use File → Import → Battleforge Model (.drs/.bmg) and choose the unit's .drs.
  2. Enable Animation Clips to load the clips used by this unit.
  3. Select one of the unit's meshes and make your changes.

Keep the imported rig and GameOrientation. Save a working .blend before editing. Disable Clear Existing Content to keep existing models and Actions, including those in other scenes. Advanced Import Options → Other Clips in Folder also loads nearby SKAs that this unit does not reference. Leave it off unless you need them.

  1. Prepare your meshes and select them.
  2. Open DRS Editor → Model Setup → Set Up Model and choose Unit.
  3. Create Armature_Collection inside this model and put your deform rig there. Before weighting, parent it to GameOrientation using Object (Without Inverse); use local location/rotation 0 and scale 1.
  4. Bind the meshes to that rig and weight them.

Starting with a compatible imported skeleton is useful when reusing game animations.

  1. Import the model using Blender's importer for its format.
  2. Select its meshes and use Set Up Model → Unit.
  3. Prepare an export deform rig as described under New unit. Keep the foreign rig as your source; transfer weights and retarget its animation to the prepared rig.
  4. Parent the meshes to the export rig with Keep Transform and check their Armature modifiers. Bake the motion onto its deform bones.
  5. Create DRS materials for its meshes using the Material Guide.

Bake control-rig and constraint-driven motion onto the deform bones before export. Keep the original file as your editable source.

GameOrientation

GameOrientation converts between Blender and game coordinates. Leave this helper unchanged. Parenting a rig or mesh to it can visibly rotate the object. Use Keep Transform if you want to keep its current placement. Keep weighted meshes attached to their armature; do not reparent them all directly to GameOrientation.

Use Model Setup → Model Size to resize the whole unit. 0.5 halves it; 2 doubles it. Play its animations afterward. External effect assets keep their own dimensions.

docs.title: 2. Check the mesh and weights
docs.text:
Use the Object Guide for mesh, UV, material and collision setup. Each skinned mesh needs an Armature modifier targeting the deform rig, with vertex groups matching its bones.

Open Animation Set Editor → Skinning → Check Skin Weights. Fix unweighted vertices, keep at most four bone influences per vertex, and normalize the weights. The result buttons select affected vertices for editing. Run the check again after making changes.

Before animating a new rig, set its deform bones to Quaternion (WXYZ) rotation. Animate the deform bones rather than moving the armature object or GameOrientation. SKA exports bone location and quaternion rotation. Animated bone scale and Euler-only rotation curves are not exported; use Model Size for a uniform resize of the whole unit. Existing Euler animation needs conversion or rebaking, not just a rotation-mode switch.

docs.title: 3. Assign animations
docs.text:
1. Open DRS Editor → Animation Set Editor.
  2. For a new unit, click Init (or Initialize Animation Set), choose Unit, then OK.
  3. Choose Idle, select a variant and assign its Animation (SKA).
  4. Assign your Walk, Run, Spawn and Die Actions where needed.
  5. Open Clip Settings → Edit Settings to check duration, FPS and looping.
  6. Check each animation with Play, then click Save.

Keep a working Base Idle. Several missing animations fall back to it.

The starter entries are unassigned. Add Ability adds attack, cast or other mappings used by the unit's existing gameplay setup. It does not create a new gameplay ability. Imported units can have more entries than a new starter set.

For alternative Idle animations, add variants and use weights such as 80 / 20. Check every variant. Save stores the mappings; save your .blend too.

For attack phases, modes, release timing and IK limits, use the Animation Set Guide.

docs.title: 4. Place the unit's locators
docs.text:
Open DRS Editor → Locator Editor. Common choices are:

Locator Place it at Health Bar The desired health-bar position above the unit. Figure Hit Offset The unit's intended hit-reference point. Projectile Spawn The weapon or hand that releases the projectile. Persistent Figure FX The attachment used by a continuous effect.

Match a comparable working unit. Not every unit uses every locator.

Choose the type and Attach to, click Apply Changes, then move or rotate the helper and click Save Placement. Check bone attachments in several poses. See the Locator Guide for attachments and effect selection.

docs.title: 5. Add release markers and effects when needed
docs.text:
For an attack or spawn event, select its animation variant and click Edit Markers. Set Time between 0 and 1: 0.5 is halfway through the whole clip. Confirm with OK, preview with Display Marker, then Save.

Keep imported marker directions. For ordinary attacker-to-target pushback, use Direction 0, 0, 0. Projectile placement uses its locator.

For sounds or visual effects, use Effect Set Editor. Assign the matching Action, add an event and select a resource. Start with one variant at 100%. Click Save, then Update Preview, and press Space. Follow the Effect Set Guide for the full steps.

docs.title: 6. Export and check
docs.text:
1. Save changes in Animation Set Editor and Effect Set Editor. Save locator placement and your .blend.
  2. Run Model Setup → Check Model and fix its errors.
  3. Open File → Export → BattleForge Model (.drs) and choose Unit.
  4. Enable Include Animation Files to include the referenced clips.
  5. Fix any Export Check errors, then export to a separate output folder. If an included clip is missing, load it or restore its source file.
  6. Reimport the exported copy in a new scene. Check the whole animation and its loop.
  7. Test movement, attacks, attachments and effects in the Map Editor.

Keep exported DRS, texture and SKA filenames together. Install custom effects and sounds separately; the DRS stores their references.

Advanced: animation export

Bake IK, constraints and NLA results onto the deform rig before exporting. Do not export the control rig as the game skeleton. Check the exported SKA by importing it again, especially after changing the rest pose or retiming.

For cubic animation, prefer aligned curve handles and check the motion between keys after reimport. Blender's independent incoming and outgoing handles cannot both be stored as one SKA tangent.

Include Animation Files includes saved AnimationSet, marker and EffectSet references. It does not export every unrelated Action in your .blend. Check the filename-prefix options rather than renaming exported SKAs by hand.

If something looks wrong Problem Check The rig plays correctly but export does not Bake the deform Action and reimport the exported SKA. An attachment returns to its old position Click Save Placement in Locator Editor. An Action is missing from export Assign it in the intended editor and Save before exporting. Movement slides along the ground Check the clip's Walk / Run Reference Speed against its authored motion. The whole animation faces the wrong way Check the rig's parent and rest pose before changing GameOrientation.
